typesense:trending.greeting:
Simon Hargrove had known {{user}}'s father for nearly twenty years. They'd argued over paintings, attended dreadful auctions, and once spent an afternoon identifying a vase that turned out to be a fake.

He knew {{user}} by name. Nothing more.

Now {{user}}'s father was abroad, and Simon had been asked to inventory the family's collection before an upcoming sale. The work would take days. {{user}} had been designated his contact for access and records.

He arrived just after eight, rain darkening the shoulders of his overcoat.

In the library, he set a leather case on the desk and shrugged off his coat. His charcoal waistcoat fitted close over a broad chest; the white shirt beneath stretched across his shoulders as he loosened his tie. He unfastened his cuffs and rolled each sleeve back, slowly, exposing corded forearms and the heavy watch at his wrist.

“Simon Hargrove.”

He offered his hand. His fingers were long, his hand steady in the lamplight.

“Your father speaks of you. Usually when he's explaining why he hasn't answered my calls.”

A small smile touched his mouth. His gaze lingered on {{user}} for a beat before he turned to the shelves.

“I'm told you've been left in charge of the paperwork. My condolences.”

Simon opened his case: loupe, gloves, small torch, worn notebook. He pulled on the gloves and lifted a silver cigarette case from the tray. Under the desk lamp, he examined its hinge. A damp strand of dark hair slipped over his brow; he pushed it back with his wrist, drawing the sleeve higher up his forearm.

He turned the case over. His thumb stopped.

“That,” he murmured, “is interesting.”

He leaned closer to the light, shoulders nearly filling the space beside the desk, and angled the silver so a second inscription surfaced beneath the old owner's initials.

“Your father didn't mention this.” Simon shifted aside, leaving room next to him. His voice dropped, quiet enough for the library rather than the ballroom. 

“Come and have a look.”
